post.summary:
Drafts a mapping or a manifest with the assistant: the model is asked, its answer validated
with the rules a save applies, and problems are fed back for at most `ai.max_repair_attempts`
repairs. The answer is the validated draft with its diff against the saved version and a dry
run, or the last problems. Only a validated draft can be accepted. Workspace admins who are
signed in; an API key is refused. Every attempt is a gated model call: it counts against the
budget and the rate limit, and with the assistant off, nothing is read or sent. A reverse
proxy in front needs a read timeout of at least (1 + `ai.max_repair_attempts`) x 60 s + 30 s.

429.description: Too many AI calls (`ai_rate_limited`); try again in a minute

post.summary:
Creates a contact. The write applies in this request: the answer is the stored contact.
Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 characters) to make a retry safe: the same key
with the same request replays the first status and the contact as stored now, and writes
nothing; the same key with another request is refused with `422` and the code
`idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are remembered for 24 hours. Without the header, an
identical repeat is a no-op because a write that changes nothing stores nothing, but a
repeated create is answered `409`.

parameters.description: 1 to 255 characters; makes a retry safe for 24 hours

post.summary:

a session may use it too, with the CSRF token. Sending is limited per API key (per user for
a session) at the ingestion rate, and the body at the ingestion size.

get.summary:
Watches the workspace's events as they are decided: one `item` frame per outcome
(`accepted`, `flagged`, `unplanned`, `rejected` or `duplicate`), live, with no
history beyond the last few seconds before it connected (so a batch that was still
committing is not missed). Each frame's `id` is a position that is safe to resume from: send it back as
`Last-Event-ID` and the stream continues after it, possibly repeating a few rows the
client already has (their `seq` identifies them). A position beyond the feed (the feed is
unlogged and starts over after a crash) is clamped to its end and announced with a `gap`
frame whose `reset` is true. A viewer that cannot keep up gets an `event: gap` frame with
the number of rows skipped (an upper bound when filters apply). While the server's
notifier is down, an `event: status` frame says `degraded` and the stream polls every few
seconds instead of reacting at once; another says it recovered.
get.description:
While at least one viewer watches a workspace, ingestion writes a feed row per event;
when none does, it writes nothing extra. Values are masked per viewer as in the person
timeline; `reveal=true` shows the stored (redacted) values to a viewer who may see values
(owner, workspace admin or `admin` key) and is ignored for anyone else. A workspace has at
most 20 streams per server process; more get 429 with `Retry-After`. Streams end when the
server shuts down.

parameters.description: Show stored values to a viewer who may see values; default false

Uploads a CSV file as a new import. The body is the raw `text/csv` file, streamed into the
database in 1 MiB chunks; it must be UTF-8 (a byte order mark is ignored) with a header row

fix. It is recorded on the `event.replayed` decisions.

and the run resumed from its checkpoint.

`stream_settings_invalid`, `source_error` or `job_failed`; never a value.

sample.description:

records.description: The records exactly as the API returned them (raw values, before any mapping).

q.description:

person with that email or phone.

deps.description:

change classes.

last.description: ISO 8601 duration in days or hours, such as P90D.

evidence.description:
What proves the decision, such as `ip`, `user_agent`, `form` or `text`. A JSON object
of at most 4 KiB as compact JSON.

oauth.description: The OAuth2 consent state; never a token.

there; the server never fetches it.
